segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, um, so I think we're all here.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: This is our third meeting, the conceptual design one.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So, uh, agenda. First the dishwasher test, then Jonas's sketches, and then we decide the concept, so materials, shape, the logo and so on.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Oh, and I sent the minutes from last time round on Wednesday, did everyone get them?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, got them.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And I sent my notes from the fair round too, finally.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yes, thanks Marta, they were really useful.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Um, before we start, sorry, can I just, my laptop's still doing an update.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Sure, no problem.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Wasn't it your race on Sunday, Jonas?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, the half marathon, in the end.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Oh, how did it go?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Um, okay, I did it in just under two hours.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: That's great!

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: The last five kilometres were awful though, it was raining the whole time.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: I did one years ago and I couldn't walk for three days.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, the stairs on Monday were, uh, not fun.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Are you doing another one?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Maybe in spring, there's one along the river in April.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: You should get Priya to run it with you.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Ha, no. Absolutely not.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay, it's back. Sorry.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Right, okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So Tom, the dishwasher test. How did it go at Café Lindner?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, so, Marta set it up with the owner, Mr Lindner, the week after our last meeting.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: He was really happy to do it actually.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: I took twelve polypropylene samples, and they ran for the whole week with his normal loads.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: He reckons that's about a hundred and forty cycles.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And the cups themselves are fine. No warping, no cracks, the rim's still round.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Uh, the lids still fit, I checked every one at the end.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Oh nice.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: But, um, the logo. I'd pad printed a test logo on the side, and that faded quite badly.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: On some of them you could barely read it after the week.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Hmm. So what are the options there?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: The main alternative is in-mould labelling. The label goes into the mould and gets fused into the wall.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: So it can't wash off, basically.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And what does that cost?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: About fifteen cents more per cup, so we'd be at roughly one thirty-five.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: That's still well under three euros.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And the logo is really important for the cafes, that was the number one thing in my notes.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So are we happy to go with in-mould labelling?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Definitely.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, polypropylene confirmed then, with an in-mould label for the logo.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: The other thing I noticed at Lindner's is it gets quite hot to hold.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: So I'd suggest a ribbed band moulded round the middle, so you've got a grip and you don't need a cardboard sleeve.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Oh that's good, because cafes hate stocking sleeves.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Does that change the cost?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Not really, it's just in the mould. Maybe a cent or two.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Does it still stack though? With the ribs?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, the band sits on the outside, the taper's the same, so they still nest.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So the ribbed band is in. Good.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: What about size? Marta, what did the cafes say?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Um, most of them sell a regular at about three hundred millilitres.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: But a few wanted a large as well, so I wondered if we do two sizes.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: The thing is, a second size means a second mould, and the rim might not be ninety mill anymore.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, and we agreed in the last meeting that the ninety millimetre rim was a must, for the lids.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Oh, true, true.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So I'd say one size, three hundred mil, for the launch, and we look at a large one later.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, yeah, that makes sense for now.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Fine by me.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And colour?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I thought maybe each cafe could pick its own colour? Like their brand colour.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Hmm, but the cups go from cafe to cafe. You'd return a pink cup to a cafe with green ones.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And people need to recognise it's the deposit cup, wherever they are.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, okay, fair point.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I'd go for one neutral base colour so the logo stands out. Like a slate grey.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Grey's easy, and it hides coffee staining better than white.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Everyone okay with slate grey?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, slate grey, one colour for every cafe.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, Jonas, your sketches.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, so, this is the counter return flow.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: The customer brings the cup to any partner cafe and hands it over at the counter.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Staff do a quick check, just that it's not cracked, and they give the euro back.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: But I added one thing. If the customer is buying another drink anyway, they just swap.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Dirty cup in, clean cup out, no deposit changes hands.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Oh, I like that. That's exactly the no-extra-steps thing the owners wanted.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: What if the cup is cracked?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Then they still refund it, I think, otherwise there's an argument at the counter.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, I'd rather not have staff arguing over a euro.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So, refund or swap at the counter. Are we agreed?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: And here's the badge. It's a round window sticker, slate grey now I guess, with the cup outline and the same logo as on the cup.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: That looks good. Maybe make the logo bigger, you need to see it from the street.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, I can do that.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, so the badge in slate grey with the matching logo, and Jonas makes the logo bigger.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Then the lost cups. With the label the cup's about one thirty-five.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So now a cafe loses about thirty-five cents on every cup that doesn't come back, not twenty.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Mr Lindner asked about that as well actually.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Well, easy, we just put a GPS tracker in every cup. Still under three euros, no problem.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Ha, and then we bring the app back.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, sure, solid gold cups next.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, okay.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: No but seriously, I think the company should cover it, maybe out of a small partner fee.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Hmm, that's not really our call though. That's a management decision.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I'll raise it with management this week and see if they'd absorb it.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Right, um, so for the next meeting, that's the detailed design.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Tom, can you get a quote for the in-mould label and the ribbed band?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, I'll ask the moulding company for a quote on the three hundred mil cup with both.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And Jonas, the bigger logo on the badge.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Sure. And I could also write a little one-page guide for staff, how the refund and the swap work.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Actually, can I do that one? I know the cafe owners, I could write it how they'd say it, and run it past Mr Lindner.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Oh yeah, that's better, go for it.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, so the staff guide is Marta's then.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And I'll check the slate grey with Mr Lindner too while I'm at it.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Great.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And I'll do the minutes, as usual, and the management question.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Anything else?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Do we need more samples for the detailed design?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Let's see what the quote says first.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, thanks everyone, see you next week.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Thanks.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Bye.

abstract: The project manager opened the conceptual design meeting and confirmed that the minutes and the marketing expert's trade fair notes had been sent round.

The industrial designer reported on the week-long dishwasher test at Café Lindner, which the marketing expert had arranged: twelve polypropylene samples went through about 140 cycles with no warping or cracks and the lids still fit, but the pad-printed test logo faded badly.
The team confirmed polypropylene and chose in-mould labelling for the logo, which brings the cup to about 1.35 euros, and added a moulded ribbed grip band instead of a cardboard sleeve.
The team settled on a single 300 ml size with the 90 mm rim for launch and a single slate grey colour for all cafes, rejecting cafe-specific colours.
The user interface designer presented the counter return flow, including a swap option for customers buying another drink, and the slate grey partner badge, both of which were accepted.
With the higher cup cost, a cafe now loses about thirty-five cents per unreturned cup, and the project manager will take the question of who covers this to management.

decisions: Polypropylene is confirmed as the cup material after the Café Lindner dishwasher test.

There will be one size of 300 ml with the 90 mm rim for launch; a large size may be looked at later.
All cups will be one neutral slate grey colour, the same for every cafe.
At the counter, staff either refund the one-euro deposit or swap a used cup for a clean one when the customer buys another drink; cracked cups are still refunded.
The partner badge will be a round slate grey window sticker with the cup outline and the same logo as on the cup.
problems: Cafes now lose about thirty-five cents per unreturned cup; whether the company will cover this (for example through a partner fee) is a management decision still pending.
Whether to offer a large size later is still open.
The actual cost of the in-mould label and ribbed band still has to be confirmed by the manufacturer's quote, and whether more samples are needed depends on it.
